q: What two things does every recursive function need?
options: A base case that stops it, and a call on a smaller problem
A return type and a name
why: Without the base case it never stops. Without a smaller problem it never gets closer to the base case.

q: Why is plain recursive `fib(40)` slow, and what fixes it?
options: The numbers get too big; use BigInt
It solves the same sub-problems again and again; remember each answer (memoization)
Recursion is always slow; use a loop only
The call stack is too small; raise the limit
why: `fib(30)` made 2,692,537 calls. With a memo it made 59.

q: For dynamic programming, what must you say first about the table?
options: How big the computer memory is
why: State, start, rule, answer. If you cannot say what `dp[i]` means in words, the rule will be wrong.

q: Coins `[1, 3, 4]`, amount 6. What does greedy (biggest coin first) give, and what is the best?
options: Greedy gives 3 coins (4+1+1); the best is 2 coins (3+3)
why: Greedy looks only at the best choice now. DP tries every choice, so it finds 3 + 3.

q: In backtracking subsets, why `result.push([...path])` and not `result.push(path)`?
options: `path` is one array that keeps changing, so every result would point at the same array
why: I ran the wrong version on `[1, 2]` and got `[[],[],[],[]]`.

q: A question asks for the NUMBER of ways (or the fewest). A different one asks to LIST all ways. Which tools?
why: Backtracking lists everything, so it costs O(2ⁿ) or O(n!) at worst. A count can often be done with a small table.
